APPROVE — bounded independent UI-D S1 runtime review at 8b58a6a6f3f975af0ecb744ddec7e7d59c1d92e3, tree880432f6305b1b003c21dbf1827dc93a64db64b1, base combined3c82d83b0c807f41a9a26308285552d7221d4804. Production sources unchanged in detached .claude/worktrees/review-ui-d-s1-8b58a6a. This verdict covers the assigned S1 delta and does not assert a clean full-range Studio wire contract.

Independent runtime evidence:
- Fresh IndependentUiDS1ReviewSuite passes4/4 on JVM and4/4 on JS. Its exhaustive oracle checks256 subsets with injected duplicate keys, offscreen trials, unmatched participants and ignored phases at3 page sizes (768 complete count traversals per platform), exact matched/control/query/map totals over3 scales, and unresolved None versus completed zero counts.
- StudyWork.scala:87 retains matched-only cardinality. A fresh matrix spans1..3 matched references and larger control sets, 46 distinct selected-budget combinations and3 quantum sizes, checking exact first excess and matched RequireOne refusal precedence; separate matched overflow remains a typed schedule refusal. No reliance on the implementation to compute the independent pair-count oracle.
- StudyWork.scala:118 and CountCursor.scala:128 reject changed input and changed plan choices with exact error operands, while separately rebuilt equal inputs/choices accept their counts.
- Diagnose.scala:205 and StageMeter.scala:91 project64 cases per platform (all4 stages x4 units x4 error cases) with exact Long.MinValue/Long.MaxValue operands, structured Exact/AtMost totals, kind/unit tokens, stable codes, severity and original messages.
- Protocol.scala:155-175: literal old Exact/AtMost/Unknown wire encodings and new Counting remain distinct. All117 existing ProtocolPins strings are independently byte-identical to base3c82d83; only total.Counting is added. All9 original ProtocolCodecSuite checks pass on each platform, alongside the new literal-wire test.

Inherited finding F1 — tracked separately as bd-01M3FMSXGEGG0BMXPWRT1168MA:
Protocol.scala:212-218 uses numeric JSON for the full accepted Long range. Actual JSON text parsing on Scala.js silently rounds9007199254740993 to9007199254740992 and rejects Long.MaxValue at .done, for both legacy Unknown and new Counting. JVM preserves both. In-memory Json.as passes, explaining the gap in existing roundtrip tests. Counted/StageMeter type, constructor, validator, encoder and decoder are byte-identical to base3c82d83 (wire-source-classification.json). This classification is based on runtime legacy-path reproduction plus exact source identity; a separate base binary was not run. Retained failing tests are not weakened or counted as passing. This inherited issue is not a new S1 regression; owner should choose a compatible wire policy separately.

Commands and raw receipts (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, JDK25, sbt -J-Xmx8g):
1. planJVM/testOnly *IndependentUiDS1ReviewSuite; planJS/testOnly *IndependentUiDS1ReviewSuite; studioCoreJVM/testOnly *IndependentCountingWireReviewSuite *ProtocolCodecSuite; studioCoreJS/testOnly same. independent-runtime.log/meta: exit1,273.862425s;29/30 pass,0 ignored. Sole failure is F1 Counting Long.MaxValue on JS.
2. studioCoreJVM/testOnly *IndependentWireRangeClassificationSuite; studioCoreJS/testOnly same. wire-range-classification.log/meta: exit1,22.382351s; JVM10/10, JS6/10,0 ignored. Four expected-contract failures reproduce F1 for Unknown/Counting at2^53+1 and Long.MaxValue. Negative text decode and safe-boundary cases pass. Both logs retain the pre-existing no-tag git-describe message; no Scala compile warning failure.

Evidence directory /private/tmp/eyes4s-ui-d-review-8b58a6a holds all3 probe sources, complete logs/meta, legacy-pin-comparison.json, wire-source-classification.json, issue body and hashes. No author files edited, no status/ownership changes, merge/push, API audit, full gate or consumer publication. CountCursor.scala:25 explicitly leaves bulk cardinality finalization unbounded; S3 remains open. S2 canonical stamp and full-ticket acceptance are not claimed. Required final landing/API/consumer gates remain with author/lead.
